name: Intermittent duty-cycle operation
conditions: Energy is available only in bounded periodic windows and usable work can fit or checkpoint across them.

name: Cryptographic trust basis withdrawn
conditions: Primitives used to justify identity, secrecy or signatures are practically broken and old proofs have no independent anchor.
feedback: New signatures using the same broken basis cannot repair old authenticity; no attractor is implied.
entry: Practical breaks invalidate the assumptions under historical evidence or encrypted archives.
exit: Independent provenance and a newly trusted channel establish a limited fresh baseline; old secrecy cannot be retroactively restored.
survives: Physical custody evidence and plaintext whose integrity can be established independently, if any.
lost: Former cryptographic assurances; actual forgery or disclosure still requires a separate occurrence.
falsifier: An unaffected independent trust basis already proves the claims at issue.

kind: absorbing loss within stated system boundary
conditions: All relevant devices, copies, keys where indispensable, and independent memories or reconstruction sources are gone.

entry: Universal erasure or loss of the last usable content and indispensable decoding knowledge.
exit: None within the premise; an independent surviving source would falsify total loss, not emerge from it.

lost: Identity, history, content, permissions and ability to recognize restoration of this system.
falsifier: Any independently usable source of the purportedly vanished information exists.

name: Stale history mistaken for current permission
conditions: A stale snapshot or unrefreshed local authority state is treated as current, and later revocations or effects are missing from every check used at dispatch.
feedback: Local checks keep validating the stale account; repeated restores or continued failed updates can repeat the mistake, but one stale check is a transient hazard.
entry: Old token or queued task becomes actionable after restore, or a role change or revocation never becomes effective in the state consulted by dispatch.
exit: Independent current authority and participant outcomes contradict and replace the stale dispatch premise.

lost: Fresh authorization and at-most-once effect claims across the snapshot boundary.
falsifier: A freshness or participant check outside the restored state rejects the stale credential or already executed operation.
evidence: Conditional hypothesis; no empirical attractor established. Static transition support is limited to the referenced functions; other branches are qualitative and design is not implementation.

lost: Startup of the cycle and all dependent functions.

conditions: Required data cannot be read with any currently known surviving copy, key and decoder combination, while traces of the system still exist.
